Messages.Author: tzimisce_dragon
Messages.Body:
Can Tier of Souls target an ally ?
some people in the playgroup said that
it cannot as allies don't have blood, but life.
Others said that whatever targets a minion's blood
can target an ally's life. What really happens ?

tzimisce dragon

Messages.Author: Fabio 'Sooner' Macedo
Messages.Body:
tzimisce_dragon escreveu:



Indeed, allies don't have blood, but life.

The only thing I'd risk saying about this right now is that allies
won't lose life to the vampire acting with Tier of Souls.

Allies ignore all "burn blood" effects entirely. [TOM 19960326]
http://groups-beta.google.com/groups?selm=4j7dhm$k...@darkstar.UCSC.EDU

The thing is that Tier talks about "a minion", not "a vampire". This
could mean you can target an ally, but it ignores the "move blood" part
and the acting minion gains the card and +1 bleed.
I vaguely recall that the Cryptic Mission action targets the
vampire/minion, not the counters in it, so it can be done on a vampire
even if the target has no blood. So I'd rule Tier of Souls as explained
above.

Fabio "Sooner" Macedo

Right, that follows from existing rulings on Jar the Soul. (I knew
there was a card with the same problem, but it took me an age to find
which one.)

http://www.white-wolf.com/vtes/index.php?line=rulings
Jar the Soul:
If an Ally is targeted, it will only be tapped - it will not lose a
blood (life) even if the superior version is used. [RTR]

Jar the Soul also targets "minion"s and causes a burn blood effect, but
can (per the above ruling) clearly be played at superior for no
additional effect against an ally.

Tier of Souls will follow the same template.

Cornercase action fun: You can use this to get +1 bleed against your
prey by targeting their ally instead of one of their Sabbat vampires to
circumvent the intercept they get from Communal Haven: Temple, for
example.

You are, I assume, thinking of the ruling on Saulot:

<http://groups.google.com/group/rec.games.trading-cards.jyhad/msg/8b4b9e
e04fc3b241?hl=en&>
***
That reads, to me, the same as what I said above -- you cannot choose
to move just one, but when you choose 2 (the only choice) and have only
one to move, then you move one. Much like stealing two blood.
***

(The whole thread has other discussion, but this is the crux - that
"move 2 blood" is similar to "steal 2 blood".)

I don't believe that "much like" officially means "follow the same rules
as", without a little extra help.

In a tournament, without additional clarification, I'd feel bound to
rule that it didn't affect allies for two reasons - it's move, not
steal; and so many other cards specify life or blood. Of course, "mis-
prints", missed intentions, and sloppy wordings abound, but I'd be
reticent to rule that this was one off the cuff.

Messages.Author: Fabio 'Sooner' Macedo
Messages.Body:
tzimisce_dragon escreveu:



I don't think the fact that it says "move blood" instead of "steal" or
"burn" makes any difference.

The reasoning behind that ruling on Jar the Soul (and Cryptic Mission)
is that the action targets the minion, not the counters. So I believe
it shouldn't matter if its a theft, a moving or a burn of life or blood
counters - the target is the minion. Since all these three cards can be
played on a minion - their texts clearly say "minion" - you should be
able to play Tier of Souls on an ally and gain +1 bleed if it passes,
and the ally doesn't lose life.

If you want to wait for LSJ to answer, that's fine - there's always
something that James or I could've missed. But I wouldn't sweat over
it.

Fabio "Sooner" Macedo

Of course, LSJ can get back and issue any ruling he find appropriate
about "move blood" effects that is not akin to "burn blood" effects.

It just happens I don't think there's any *need* to treat Tier of Souls
in a different way ;-) Of course, this is ultimately a debate on
designer's intent, which only LSJ can rule about. But personally, I see
these rulings on "steal" or "burn blood" as ways to emphasize that life
is one thing and blood is other - so you need explicit cardtext, errata
or rule/ruling to be able to affect both equally with the same effect.

The "steal blood" strikes work differently as stated in the rulebook,
yes, but it has been probably so Thaumaturgy doesn't suck even more ;-)

>this i disagree with. there's a ruling that allies ignore 'burn blood'
>effects. there is no such parallel ruling for 'move blood' effects.

Does there need to be?

Allies don't have blood. Vampires without blood would ignore a move
blood or burn blood effect. Why wouldn't vampires without blood do the
same?

The only reason allies are vulnerable to "steal blood" is because
there's a very specific part of the rulebook on that.

Would you need a ruling to prevent allies being susceptible to "Take
three blood counters from the opposing minion and juggle with them for a
laugh"?

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
tzimisce_dragon wrote:
> Ok with "steal blood" and "burn blood", i am asking about the "move blood"
> of tier of souls.... so, what does really happen ????????
> no life lost and acting minion wears the card and gets the +1 bleed ?

Exactly correct.

Tier of Souls may target an ally (any minion).
The "move blood" effect will have no effect, since the ally has no blood to
move.
The acting vampire wears the card and gets +1 bleed.
